scope: Continuum step 5 (base .gravity runtime and measured BASE_TRUE_TPS) -- what the required list still lacks, established by reading the runtime against the real General-R0 artifact rather than against its own documentation.

gaps.finding: The GPU weight cache is an unbounded HashMap<String, GpuTensor>. Its own doc comment states the design: uploads each tensor on first use and 'keeps it there for the life of the model'. There is no eviction, no byte budget, and no residency accounting.
gaps.why_the_assumption_fails: The comment justifies unboundedness with 'a short run touches 8 of 256 experts per layer, so most of the artifact is never uploaded at all'. That holds for a short run and fails for a real one: token-to-token routing diversity means the resident set grows monotonically toward the whole artifact.

quantified_against_the_real_artifact.worst_case_new_bytes_per_token_note: 78 layers x 8 experts/token x 3 projections x 1.378 MB
quantified_against_the_real_artifact.consequence: On a 96 GiB unified-memory host already sharing RAM with other work, an unbounded resident set reaches tens of GB within the first tens of tokens and then exhausts memory or swaps. This is consistent with BASE_TRUE_TPS having been measured over only 12 decode tokens.

gaps.fix_shape: Byte-budgeted LRU under the existing mutex. The lock is already held across dispatch_pq_matvec_batch, so no eviction can race an in-flight encode; the one real hazard is evicting a tensor that an earlier ensure() in the SAME batch just inserted, so admission must pin the current call set. Budget should be explicit and reported, not inferred.
gaps.status: QUEUED -- not implemented in this session. A Metal residency change cannot be honestly verified while PASS3 owns the machine, and shipping unverified GPU memory management would trade a known-good path for an unmeasured one.

gaps.finding: BASE_TRUE_TPS is currently a cold-start number only. Both arms run 12 decode tokens from an empty cache, so every measured token pays first-touch disk read, hash verification, and device upload for essentially every expert it routes to. No warm or steady-state number exists.

evidence.recorded_finding: SHA-256 verification of cold-touched tensors dominates: disabling it cut prefill 4.4x and decode 3.6x

gaps.interpretation: Because the cache memoizes per tensor name, hash verification is a once-per-tensor warm-up cost, not a per-token steady-state cost. The measured 3.6x is therefore a warm-up penalty being reported as a decode penalty. The honest scoreboard needs both numbers and the residency curve between them.
gaps.status: QUEUED -- requires an idle box; 81 GB working set cannot be measured while PASS3 and MOP hold the machine.

explicitly_not_claimed: That the runtime is wrong. It is correct; it is unbounded.
That warm TPS will be good. It is unmeasured, and modelled TPS is not measured TPS.
Any statement about output quality, divergence, or capability. This is F0 physical and timing only.
next_action: After PASS3 finalizes and the box is idle: implement the byte-budgeted LRU (G1), then measure cold, warm, and the residency curve on the same artifact (G2), and only then update BASE_TRUE_TPS.
not_evidence_of: output divergence, capability, or end-to-end behaviour
